method: Claude wrote one short question for the student per misconception tag that the generators or the answer checker can produce (82 tags). The practice page shows it after a wrong try with that tag. Each question points at the likely mistake without giving the answer away.

misconception_updates.look_again: Does that box need one wire on, or both wires on?
Did you keep your count going all the way to the end of the belt?
Say one clue in full words: how many symbols are in exactly the right spot, and how many are in a wrong spot?
Pick a symbol your code shares with a guess. Is it on the same wheel in both, or a different one?
Find a brick that rests on two different colours. Can it match either of them, or must it be the third colour?
The question counts only crossings with the fewest planks. Did some of yours cost more?
Two routes can pass the same corners in a different order. Are you counting routes or corners?
Does each reading you counted use up the whole signal, right to the last flash?
The box numbers are printed above the row. Which end does box 1 sit at?
Count the blocks the robot drives along, not the corners it passes.
Name each tank you counted and say its colour at the end. Is any of them mud?
Add each route up exactly. Does every one you counted match the cheapest total?
Some people hear the news from two friends. Did you tick each person only once?
Read the question again. Does the person with the news count as hearing it?
Does every necklace you counted have exactly the number of beads asked for?
Are 'east, fog' and 'fog, east' the same message? Count each order on its own.
Equal totals are not enough. Do any bolts arrive before there is a nut for them?
Point to every walkway on your route as you add. Did you count the ones touching the shores?
Turn your answer back into flashes. Is it as long as the signal?
The bulb lights. Could it light with fewer buttons pressed?
A route with fewer walkways can still need more planks. Did you add up the numbers?
Could a zigzag route be just as short?
Find an orange tank and a blue tank joined by a pipe. What does each push into the other next minute?
Could the signal start with a different first word?
Paint moves through one pipe each minute. How far can it get in the first minute?
Point to every brick of that colour, starting with the bottom row. Did you count them all?
Is there a die the rules never look at? How many faces could it show?
What colour is the tank the paint was poured into?
Work backward: which box in the outer row holds the target?
Each rule changes only the kind of object on its left side. Was it that kind?
Work backward: which rule could have made the end of this necklace? Undo it and keep going.
A rule's new objects always come out in the order shown. Did you keep that order?
Read the rule again. Which end do the new beads go on?
Picking the cheapest walkway each time doesn't work from the south shore either. Add up the whole route.
The cheapest first walkway is not always part of the cheapest crossing. Where did it lead you?
Write how far each corner is from the start, nearest first. Is heading straight for the goal really shortest?
Cross out every closed corner first. Can a route go through one?
Trace your route with a finger. Does it go through a closed corner?
When the belt is empty, how many nuts are still in the bucket?
Number the dice 1, 2, 3 from the left before you check any test. Did you use the right die each time?
Which part can you work out right now? Start with the innermost brackets.
You found a box in the outer row. Where does that box number come from in the inner row?
A new friend also tells all of their own friends. Whose friends cover everyone who is missed?
Run the count from the start. Does a bolt ever arrive with no nut waiting?
Read the question again. Does it ask how long the best route is, or how many best routes there are?
When a run of nuts starts, are some nuts already in the bucket?
Find a brick that rests on two bricks of the same colour. Does the rule let all three be the same?
Write 'minute 1', 'minute 2' and so on, with what changes under each. How many minutes does the question ask about?
Write the signal as S and L letters first. Did you read every flash right?
At each spot in the signal, did you try every code word, even the shortest one?
Count two steps out from the person with the most friends. Does that really reach the most people?
Read the rule about mud again. Can a mud tank push paint anywhere?
Does any rule say you must always head south? Try a route that steps back north.
Is there another set of buttons that also works? Try listing them in order.
Is there a different route with exactly the same total?
The friends hear it first. What does each of them do with the news next?
Did you count the friends who heard it first, as well as the people they told?
Mark where each word starts in the signal, left to right. Are your words in that order?
Which rows are odd, and which columns are odd? Look where they cross.
Every column is even now. Count each row too, including the check column on the right.
The corner shelf belongs to both the last row and the last column. Does it work for both?
A rubbed-out dot leaves an empty shelf. Can it be a shelf that still shows a dot?
Every row is even now. Count each column too, including the check row at the bottom.
Mark the friends, then their friends. Does anyone tell the news a third time?
Is your answer the box's number, or what is written inside the box?
The starting tanks follow the same rules as every other tank. What flows into each of them, and when?
Read each test out loud with the real numbers in it. Which die has to be bigger?
Before each step, which row's name is in front of the bracket?
Both colours move in the same minute. Colour both of them for minute 1, then minute 2.
Trace your route with a finger from shore to shore. Does it really connect?
After fixing the early bolts, are any nuts still left in the bucket at the end?
Only the nut on top of the pile can be taken. Does each bolt fit the nut on top?
Test your code against every clue, ticking each one off. Does it really agree with all of them?
One guess has nothing right. Did you cross out every symbol in it?
To reach that line, an earlier test had to be false. Did you check it?
Count the pairs of brackets. Each pair is one lookup. Did you do them all?
Two of the dice are equal. Is 'greater than' true when the numbers are the same?
Write the number of nuts in the bucket under each part. Does a bolt ever find it empty?
Bolts take nuts out as the belt moves. Follow the bucket after each part.
Does the rule add both beads to one end, or one bead at each end?
What does an 'only one' box do when both of its wires are on?
Read the small number above each box. Which box is box 1?
